new_helpers.name: low_variance_sites

new_helpers.name: median_mad_threshold
new_helpers.what: median + lambda * MAD upper-tail threshold; ops.robust.robust_z returns 1.4826-scaled z-scores and needs n >= 5, not the raw median/MAD scale

new_helpers.name: spike_statistic
new_helpers.what: Eq (2) itself (max * log(1 + max/mean) over the per-token magnitudes), not a library gap

deviations: The paper's setting is a serving platform that gates one downloaded third-party adapter per user prompt; this port mounts the detector at SERVER_RECEIVE and inspects each client upload as the adapter under inspection, the reading the built-in ComplianceProbe gives an upload. That analogy is mine, not the paper's.

The prompts to judge arrive as a defender-supplied resource (screen_prompts) instead of at generation time, because fedguard has no inference stage; the same per-adapter threshold is applied to that fixed batch.
The clean and screening prompt sets are the defender's own; the paper's 40 Alpaca prompts are a reported scale, not a constant baked into the plugin.
Verdicts are report-only: flagged prompts appear by index in scores/features/evidence and nothing is blocked (see missing_runtime).

Setup is recomputed whenever the uploaded factors change (fingerprint: entry count + sum of all factor values), so the plugin re-reads the adapter each round; the paper computes the setup once per adapter offline.
The paper's serving cost (one forward pass per prompt) is preserved only for the screening batch; calibration adds one pass per clean prompt the first time an adapter is seen.
open_choices: activation magnitude = L2 norm of the raw A-side bottleneck output, with no alpha/r scaling (magnitude="l1" switches to the L1 norm). The paper only writes activation magnitude.
sigma_m = sample standard deviation (ddof=1); a site with a single clean prompt gets 0.

bd_k is the raw MAD (no 1.4826 factor), which is what makes lambda = 4.45 equal to the three Gaussian-consistent MAD units the paper mentions; the median is the 0.5 quantile (ops.robust.coordinate_median), i.e. the mean of the two middle values for an even count.
|M_k| = max(1, round-half-up(k * |M|)) and sigma ties are broken by site order in sorted state-dict order; the paper gives neither rule.

A selected site with sigma <= 1e-12 is dropped from the average instead of contributing an undefined z-score; n_selected and n_monitored report the difference, and with no monitored site nothing is screened.
Module-name mapping: <site>.lora_A and <site>.lora_A.default are both offered; sites the handle does not report are listed as unmatched instead of failing.
Adapter identity for the once-per-adapter setup = (number of state entries, sum of all factor values); two adapters with the same sum would share a setup.

The calibration forward pass runs with the uploaded adapter loaded by the handle (the paper's wording about reading the LoRA down-projection implies it but does not state it); an adapter that is not active reports nothing and is recorded as unmatched.

A client-side mount at CLIENT_PRE_TRAIN (received_model + data + the handle around the training model) is also conceivable; it was not taken because the missing piece is the same decision surface and the server-side mount matches the built-in ComplianceProbe.
needs_from_authors: the magnitude definition of a_{m,t}(x): which norm, and whether the alpha/r scaling of Eq (1) is included
which submodules their activation capture hooks (PEFT naming and adapter-active state) and whether the setup forward runs on base+adapter or base only
the sampling of the 40 Alpaca prompts (subset, seed, dedup, length distribution) and whether they are redrawn per adapter
the rounding rule for |M_k|, the sigma estimator (ddof), and whether bd_k is multiplied by 1.4826
how a single prompt's statistics are isolated under continuous batching and how over-long prompts are truncated
confidence_reason: The six ported steps run green against the real GuardRunner/OpenFedLLMGuard and the harness (9 tests, synthetic activations, no model): the low-variance site selection, the trigger flag, the decoy on an unmonitored site, the reused per-adapter setup, the zero-variance degenerate case and both PEFT module spellings are all asserted. Two things were not executed: a real PEFT model (the activation route and the module-name mapping are inferred from fedguard/adapters/hf_model.py and PEFT naming, kept configurable and non-fatal), and the serving-time half, which this library cannot host. The verdict boundary is a judgement call: the detector's computation and calibration are ported and tested, the reject-before-generation gate is not.
